question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
The National Building Research Institute Act, No. 20 of 2025 — the certified Act, not a bill — gives an opting-out officer or employee **six months** from the date the offer of employment in the Institute was made [Act 20/2025 §33].

- The wording is "within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute", i.e. time runs from the offer, not from any separate notification [Act 20/2025 §33(2)(b)].
- That option applies to officers/employees of the dissolved National Building Research Organisation who were in service the day before commencement and had not reached retirement age [Act 20/2025 §33(2)(a)].
- On exercising the option not to accept, compensation is payable under a voluntary retirement scheme approved by the Minister and the Minister of Finance [Act 20/2025 §33(2)(c)].

Caveats: the Act does not use the word "notified", so the six months is measured from the offer date as stated; the section is quoted from the certified Act, and this is not legal advice.

question: Under the proposed Inland Revenue amendment, from which assessment date are deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act excluded from subsection (2)?
answer:
For any year of assessment **prior to April 1, 2018**. [Act 11/2026 §34]

- Section 34 inserts new section 202(2A), stating subsection (2) “shall not apply” where the amount was already deducted under section 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act for any year of assessment prior to April 1, 2018. [Act 11/2026 §34]
- This applies even if an un-deducted balance remains as at April 1, 2018. [Act 11/2026 §34]

Caveats: The evidence is the **certified Inland Revenue (Amendment) Act, No. 11 of 2026** (certified 2026-06-03), not the Gazette bill. [Act 11/2026 §34]

question: Under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law, how long does a licence issued or renewed remain in effect?
answer:
Under the certified **Act No. 9 of 2026** (the bill became law), the term depends on the licence: a **moneylending licence** issued under s.23 or renewed under s.24 is **valid for one year** [Act 9/2026 §25], while a **microfinance-business licence** is **issued for three years** [Act 9/2026 §32].

- The one-year rule expressly covers issue and renewal and requires an expiry date [Act 9/2026 §25].
- For microfinance licences, s.32(9) applies s.25(a),(b),(d),(e) but omits s.25(c), the one-year validity paragraph [Act 9/2026 §32].

Caveat: the question says “proposed”; the Gazette bill became Act 9/2026, so the Act wording governs [645/2025 §32].

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer:
Under the Act now in force, the renewal application must be submitted to the Director-General "not less than thirty days prior to the date of expiration of the licence previously issued" [Act 3/2026 §6(1)].

- It must be in the prescribed Form with the prescribed renewal fee [Act 3/2026 §6(1)].
- This is the certified Act (certified 2026-02-17), which came from bills 007/2026 and 657/2025 [Act 3/2026 §6].

Caveats: The 30-day period is a minimum; the Act does not state a maximum or an earlier deadline.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, what is the new maximum duration a freezing order may be in effect?
answer:
Under the certified Prevention of Money Laundering (Amendment) Act, No. 16 of 2026, the longest period a freezing order may run appears to be raised **from three months to four months**, with a related retention period going from two years to three years [Act 16/2026 §9].

- Clause §9(2)(a) substitutes "shall not exceed four months" for "shall not exceed three months" in section 8(2)(b) of the principal enactment [Act 16/2026 §9].
- Separately, the shorter period in section 7(3) is extended from "seven days" to "fourteen working days" [Act 16/2026 §8].

Caveats: the principal Act's text is not in the evidence, so whether "four months" or "fourteen working days" is the true outer limit of a freezing order cannot be confirmed; this is an amending Act, not the consolidated law.

question: Under the amended Telecommunication Levy law, how often is the levy calculated on the value of telecom services received?
answer:
Under the 2026 amendment bill, the levy is calculated on the value of telecom services supplied "in respect of each month" — i.e. monthly. [028/2026 §2]

- The levy is charged "from every person receiving any telecommunication service… at such rate as specified in the Schedule", on the value of the supply by "any operator or provider". [028/2026 §2]
- Same wording appears in the later version of the bill, 035/2026 (2026-05-06); the Gazette text is dated 2026-04-23. [028/2026 §2]

Caveats: This is a bill only — no certified Act is held, so it has not been shown to have passed; the monthly basis is what the bill proposes, not established law. [035/2026; 028/2026 §2]

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
Act 13/2025 (certified 2025-08-15) substitutes a new section 49(5) of the Bills of Exchange Ordinance (Chapter 82), allowing dishonour notice "in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means" [Act 13/2025 §8].

- Any electronic means must "sufficiently identify the bill, and intimate that the bill has been dishonoured by non-acceptance or non-payment" [Act 13/2025 §8].
- This is an amending Act, so it states the change only; the Ordinance's consolidated text is not in the evidence [Act 13/2025 §8].

Caveats: the full amended section 49 is not reproduced, so other notice rules (e.g. who must give notice, time limits) cannot be confirmed.

question: Under the proposed Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation incorporation law, who is defined as a qualified auditor?
answer:
The Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation (Incorporation) bill defines a "qualified auditor" in §11(4): an individual who is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or another institute established by law) and holds "a certified to practice as Accountant issued by the Council of such Institute", or a firm of accountants whose resident partners each meet that test [626/2025 §11].

- The audit is by a qualified auditor "appointed by Auditor General in terms of Article 154 of the Constitution" [626/2025 §11].
- This is a bill, not law: it is "Proposal, not itself law" and no certified Act is held, so it has not been shown to have passed [626/2025 §11]; the Gazette text (2025-06-19) is identical [607/2025 §11].

Caveats: The passage's wording is garbled/truncated ("possesses a certified to practice"), so the exact statutory phrasing cannot be confirmed from this evidence.

question: What is meant by “knowledge sharing activities” under the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture Act?
answer:
The evidence does not show an Act: the definition appears only in the Gazette text of the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture (Incorporation) Bill (2025-11-20), which has not been shown to have passed. There, “knowledge sharing activities” is defined as “activities designed to facilitate to exchange of ideas, skills, and experiences fostering on culture of learning and collaboration” [646/2025 §18] — i.e., activities aimed at exchanging ideas, skills and experience and building a learning, collaborative culture (my reading; the printed wording is garbled).

- It is a definition clause (“In this Act, unless the context otherwise required”) covering the same terms as “bank” and “written law” [646/2025 §18].
- Identical text also appears in 002/2026 [646/2025 §18].

Caveats: Proposed, not enacted; no certified Act was found, so this wording may not be law.

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
The bills would let the Society "take and hold any property, movable or immovable" and sell, mortgage, lease, exchange or otherwise dispose of it — but no certified Act exists, so this is proposed, not law [047/2026 §13].

- Property may come "by virtue of any purchase, grant, gift, testamentary disposition or otherwise" and must be held for the Act's purposes and subject to rules under section 7 [047/2026 §13].
- Section 6 adds powers to purchase, rent, construct, renovate and otherwise obtain lands or buildings and dispose of them as the Council determines [041/2026 §6], and to administer trusts over "any real or personal property" [041/2026 §6].
- Rules on "the administration and management of the property of the body corporate" require a two-thirds majority at a general meeting [047/2026 §7].

Caveats: Both texts (Gazette text 2026-06-11; Bill 2026-06-25) carry identical wording; neither has been shown to have passed.

question: In the Institute of Real Estate Professionals, who chairs the Membership and Policy Advisory committees, and how are chairs selected for the remaining committees?
answer:
Under the Act, the President of the Institute chairs both the Membership Committee and the Policy Advisory and Constitutional Committee [Act 6/2026 §18(2)].

- Every other committee must include at least one Council member, who is its Chairperson [Act 6/2026 §18(2)].
- Where more than one Council member sits on a committee, "the Council shall appoint one of such members as the Chairperson" [Act 6/2026 §18(3)].
- In the Chairperson's absence, members present elect one of themselves to preside [Act 6/2026 §18(5)].

This is the certified Act 6/2026 (2026-02-19), which came from bills 637/2025 and 656/2025; the earlier Gazette text said "Chairman" in subsections (2) and (5), whereas the Act uses "Chairperson".

question: Under the amended Colombo Port City Economic Commission law, how is the income tax treatment of workers hired by licensed businesses affected depending on whether the licence was granted before or after the new provisions take effect?
answer:
Under Act 1/2026 (certified), businesses licensed **before** the new section 35 commencement get a three-year employee income-tax exemption; businesses licensed **on or after** commencement are taxable.

- Pre-commencement licensees: resident employment income is “exempt from income tax” and credited to the employee’s personal foreign currency account; non-resident employment income is exempt and no Sri Lankan tax applies to foreign-earned income [Act 1/2026 §3].
- The exemption is “for a period of three years commencing from the month immediately following” commencement [Act 1/2026 §3].
- Post-commencement licensees: resident and non-resident employment income “shall be liable to income tax” [Act 1/2026 §3].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
The amendment (now **Act No. 4 of 2026**, certified 2026-02-17, not merely a bill) removes container operators from the principal Act’s long title: it substitutes “freight forwArders And non-VesseL operAting common cArriers” for “freight forwArders, non-VesseL operAting common cArriers, And contAiner operAtors” [Act 4/2026 §2].

- It separately replaces the Act’s name with “Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders and Non-Vessel Operating Common Carriers Act” in the principal enactment and other written law [Act 4/2026 §3(1)(a)].
- References in documents are to be read as references to that shortened name [Act 4/2026 §3(2)].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer:
The evidence shows the amendment makes **many separate changes** to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, No. 25 of 2005, not one single modification; its long title says only "to Amend" that Act [Act 18/2026].

- New offence provision inserted after s.3(2A) covering collection/provision of funds for terrorist training, travel to become a "foreign terrorist fighter", etc. [Act 18/2026 §4].
- Terminology replaced throughout, e.g. "funds or property" → "funds, property or other assets", and "finance business" definition repealed in s.16A [Act 18/2026 §16].
- Detention period in s.4(3) changed from "seven days" to "fourteen working days" [Act 18/2026 §5].

Caveats: no passage states an overall purpose or summary of the amendment; it is an amending Act, so the earlier Act's consolidated text is not in evidence.

question: Which 2025 bill outlines the government's budget and borrowing provisions for the financial year 2026?
answer:
The 2025 bill is **Bill 639/2025, Appropriation (Bill, 2025-09-26)**, which became **Appropriation Act, No. 23 of 2025** (certified 2025-12-05); answer from the Act.

- It authorises FY2026 expenditure of Rs 4,434,356,468,000 and borrowing, with loan details reported under s.51 of the Public Financial Management Act, No. 44 of 2024 [Act 23/2025 §2].
- The Act caps outstanding borrowing at Rs 3,740 billion [Act 23/2025 §2]; the bill had proposed Rs 3,800 billion, so that figure was not enacted [639/2025 §2].

Caveats: the Act header also links it to bill 632/2025, but only 639/2025’s text is in evidence [Act 23/2025].

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
It is the **Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation)** bill — Gazette text 043/2026 (2026-06-15) and Bill 055/2026 (2026-07-27, titled there "Recourses"). Neither is shown to have passed; no certified Act exists in the evidence.

- It incorporates the Foundation with perpetual succession, power to sue and be sued and a common seal, deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization [043/2026 §2].
- Objects include developing "all economic sectors", rural youth vocational training, micro-entrepreneurship for unemployed women, drug-abuse prevention and soil conservation [043/2026 §3].
- Implementation must be without distinction based on race, religion, caste, sex and similar grounds [043/2026 §3(2)].

Caveats: both are proposals only (Acts checked to 2026-10-30); the two titles differ in spelling ("Resources" vs "Recourses").

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media law, what is the maximum length of a suspension the Council can impose instead of disenrolling a member?
answer:
The maximum is **one year** — the Council may "suspend him from membership for such period not exceeding one year" in lieu of disenrolling him [054/2026 §24].

- The same clause also allows a warning or reprimand as alternatives, and discretionary re-enrolment [054/2026 §24].
- The power arises only where the Disciplinary Committee's report under section 23(3) establishes professional misconduct [054/2026 §24]; "professional misconduct" is defined by Council rules under section 26 [054/2026 §23].
- This is a bill, not law: it has not been shown to have passed (no certified Act as at 2026-10-30) [054/2026 §24].

Caveats: The identical text also appears in bills 040/2026 and 050/2026 ("Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka"), all dated 2026-07-22; the name in the question best matches 054/2026.

question: Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, how long must someone have continuously and peacefully occupied a premises to be regarded as an “occupant”?
answer:
Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, an "occupant" must have been in "undisturbed and uninterrupted occupation" of the premises for "a period of more than three months", in addition to being in lawful occupation [004/2026 §2].

- The newest version, the Bill of 2026-01-20, uses exactly this wording [004/2026 §2].
- The earlier Gazette text (2025-09-18) is identical: "more than three months", undisturbed and uninterrupted [634/2025 §2].

Caveats: both are bills, not law — neither has been shown to have passed (no certified Act held, checked to 2026-10-30) [004/2026 §2].

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
The evidence supports **seventy years of age**, but only as a bar to *appointment*: a person is disqualified from being appointed a member of the Board if he "is over seventy years of age" [Act 17/2025 §9(i)].

- This is from the certified **Gambling Regulatory Authority Act, No. 17 of 2025** (certified 2025-09-03), not a pending bill [Act 17/2025 §9].
- The age bar appears in the disqualification list alongside other grounds, e.g. being a member of Parliament, a Provincial Council or a local authority [Act 17/2025 §9(a)].

Caveats: No passage states an age at which a sitting member must vacate office, so the effect of reaching 70 while serving is not shown in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, what is the longest jail term a person can receive for arriving in or departing Sri Lanka with cash or bearer‑negotiable instruments above the minister‑set limit?
answer:
The longest jail term is **one year**: conviction by a Magistrate carries imprisonment “of either description for a term not exceeding one year,” or a fine, or both. [Act 17/2026 §31]

- The fine can be “three times of the value” of the cash or bearer-negotiable instruments. [Act 17/2026 §31]
- The excess cash/instruments are forfeited to the State. [Act 17/2026 §31]

This is from the certified amending **Act No. 17 of 2026**, not a bill; it substitutes section 27 of the principal Act. [Act 17/2026 §31]

question: Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket law, what penalty amount does a member owe if they fail to pay the subscription by the deadline?
answer:
Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket bill, the defaulting member owes a "late payment fee equal to twice the annual subscription" [072/2026 §30(4)].

- The subscription itself is due by 31 December of the year preceding the relevant financial year [072/2026 §30(3)]; the doubled fee is payable by 30 April of the following year [072/2026 §30(4)].
- Continued non-payment costs the member its voting right automatically and, after six months, removal from the Register of Members [072/2026 §30(5)–(6)].

Caveats: This is a Gazette text proposal (dated 2026-09-28), not shown to have passed, so these are proposed, not enacted, figures.

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
The bill fixes no payment date: it only says debts "existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act" must be paid by the body corporate — that phrase identifies *which* debts, not *when* they are due [009/2026 §12].

- Newest text: Gazette text of 5 Feb 2026 (009/2026), identical wording in the Bill of 17 Feb 2026 [014/2026 §12]; neither has been shown to have passed.
- A near-identical 2021 bill used the same formula [095/2021 §12] — different bill, so not authority for this one.

Caveats: No time limit or penalty for late payment appears in the evidence; commencement date is not stated.

question: Under the proposed Immigration Bill, what is the minimum and maximum penalty imposed on a ship's master or aircraft captain who fails to report a transit passenger or crew member that appears to have stayed in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Under the proposed Immigration Bill, the fine is **not less than LKR 100,000 and not more than LKR 500,000**, on conviction [082/2026 §90(2)].

- The offence is failing to notify an Immigration Officer that a transit passenger or crew member did not continue their journey, where it may reasonably be inferred they remained in Sri Lanka [082/2026 §90(1)–(2)].
- The master, captain **or agent** is "jointly and severally liable" [082/2026 §90(2)].

Caveats: This is a bill, not law — the text is a proposal and we hold no certified Act for it, so it has not been shown to have passed [082/2026 §90].

question: Under the proposed Convention against Doping in Sport amendment, how long does the Board Chairman serve?
answer:
Under the amendment, the Chairman "shall hold office for a term of three years and shall be eligible for reappointment" [Act 21/2025 §11].

- This is an Act (certified 2025-10-07), not a bill: it repeals and replaces section 14(1)–(2) of the Convention against Doping in Sport Act, No. 33 of 2013, with the Chairman chosen from the appointed members by majority of the ex-officio members [Act 21/2025 §11].

Caveats: The three-year term is taken from the new subsection (2) as certified; the amended Act's consolidated text is not in evidence.

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
Under the amended Rubber Control Act, "Director‑General" means the Director‑General of the Rubber Development Department, "appointed or deemed to have been appointed under this Act" [Act 16/2025 §6].

- This is the definition substituted for the repealed definition of "Controller" in section 52 of the principal enactment (Chapter 436) [Act 16/2025 §6].
- The same Act also replaces the words "Controller" and "Rubber Controller" wherever they appear, and treats references in other written laws, notices, contracts and forms as references to the "Director‑General of the Rubber Development Department" [Act 16/2025 §2].
- This is a certified Act (No. 16 of 2025, certified 2025-08-22), which amends the Rubber Control Act; it came from bills 595/2025 and 620/2025 [Act 16/2025 §6].

Caveats: The evidence is the amending Act, not the consolidated text of Chapter 436, so the Act as it now reads is not in the evidence.

question: In the amended Personal Data Protection Act, which bodies are regarded as a public authority?
answer:
Under the amendment, "public authority" means "a Ministry, any Department, Provincial Council, local authority, or a Ministry or Department of a Provincial Council", excluding public corporations and companies incorporated under the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007 [Act 22/2025 §14].

- This is a certified Act (No. 22 of 2025) that substitutes the definition in section 56 of the principal enactment, the Personal Data Protection Act, No. 9 of 2022 — so the amended Act's full text is not in the evidence [Act 22/2025 §14].
- The 2025 bill's Gazette text read "any Department or Provincial Council" rather than "any Department, Provincial Council"; the Act's wording governs [Act 22/2025 §14], [575/2025 §13].

Caveats: the passage is truncated mid-sentence after "does not include- (", so the exclusions quoted rest on the equivalent bill text and may not be complete [575/2025 §13].

question: What criteria does the amendment set for a crop to be classified as an Export Agricultural Crop?
answer:
Under the certified Act, a crop qualifies only if it has export potential alongside local consumption, is not excluded, and is declared by the Minister as a "notified agricultural crop" under section 2 [Act 24/2026 §5].

- Excluded: "paddy, vegetables, fruits, root crops and additional food crops belonging to the category of food crops", and any crop "identified as a plantation crop" [Act 24/2026 §5].
- The declaration by the Minister in charge of the subject is required; export potential alone is not enough [Act 24/2026 §5].

This is Act 24/2026 (certified 2026-10-06), which substitutes the definition in section 19 of the 1992 Act; the evidence does not include the amended Act's consolidated text.

question: Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
Under the proposed bill, a “qualified auditor” is either an individual accountant holding a practising certificate, or a firm whose resident partners each hold one.

- Individual: a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or any other institute established by law) who "possesses a certificate to practice as an Accountant", issued by that institute's Council [597/2025 §10(4)(a)].
- Firm: a firm of accountants where each resident partner is such a member and holds a certificate of practice from the Council [597/2025 §10(4)(b)].
- The audit itself is by a qualified auditor "appointed by Auditor General" under Article 154 of the Constitution [597/2025 §10(3)].

Caveats: this is the Gazette text of a proposal only — no certified Act has been shown for it. An identical text appears in 608/2025 [597/2025 header].

question: Under the proposed Proceeds of Crime Bill, what types of advanced investigative methods can an investigation officer employ with a magistrate’s permission?
answer:
Under the Proceeds of Crime Act No. 5 of 2025 — formerly bill 570/2025 and 572/2025, so it is no longer merely proposed — a Magistrate may authorize: controlled delivery; digital surveillance, including interception/recording of digital, voice and video communications; undercover operations including decoys; laying traps; and forensic extraction of data, information and images from computers, phones and other digital equipment [Act 5/2025 §60(1)].

- The Magistrate considers necessity, justification and proportionality, and may impose conditions [Act 5/2025 §60(2)–(3)].
- Progress must be reported to the Magistrate “once in fourteen days” [Act 5/2025 §60(4)].
- A separate judicial order may require activities such as forensic audit, digital forensic extraction, valuation, copying/storage of data, and forensic transaction analysis [Act 5/2025 §61].

Caveats: The bill called these “advanced investigative techniques”; the Act uses “special investigative techniques” [570/2025 §60; Act 5/2025 §60].

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka law, how many council members must be present, and must the Chairperson be among them, to constitute a quorum for a council meeting?
answer:
Five members, and the Chairperson must be one of them: the quorum is "five members including the Chairperson" [054/2026 §7(2)]. This is from a bill, not an Act — the evidence says it has not been shown to have passed [054/2026 §7].

- The same wording appears in the Gazette text of the Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka bill [040/2026 §7(2)].
- The later Bill version is titled "Establishment of the Chartered Institute of Media" though its page header reads Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka [054/2026 §7].

Caveats: No certified Act is in the evidence, so this is a proposal only.

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
Under Act 8/2025 (certified), the Commission computes fares for transport services including omnibuses using a formula it determines in line with Parliament-approved national policy, specified by Gazette Order [Act 8/2025 §19].

- The Commission’s functions include determining the fare formula after “written representations of the relevant stakeholders” and revising it after periodic assessment [Act 8/2025 §5].
- The Commission must publish fare lists on its official website [Act 8/2025 §19].
- Each operator must prepare its fare list in accordance with those website lists and display it “in a conspicuous place of the transportation vehicle”; the Commission may inspect compliance, and failure is an offence under section 40 [Act 8/2025 §19].

Caveats: This is an amending Act; the evidence does not give the section 40 penalty or further display format details.

question: According to the proposed Mass Foundation law, what continuous legal identity will the foundation have, what ability does it have to bring or face lawsuits, how can it manage its seal, and how is it classified for regulatory oversight?
answer:
It would be a body corporate with "perpetual succession" under the name "Mass Foundation", able to "sue and be sued" and to "have and use a common seal and to alter the same at its pleasure" [025/2026 §2]. This is a bill, not law: it has not been shown to have passed.

- Seal: not to be affixed except in the presence of two Committee members who sign the instrument; custody goes to an office bearer the Committee decides [025/2026 §15].
- Classification: "deemed to be a Voluntary Social Service Organization" under the Voluntary Social Service Organizations (Registration and Supervision) Act, No. 31 of 1980, whose provisions apply to its management [025/2026 §2].
- Same wording appears in the presented Bill [037/2026], 2026-05-07.

Caveats: No certified Act is held (checked to 2026-10-30), so treat all of this as proposed only.

question: Under the amendment to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Law, when a water supply and sewerage undertaking of an industrial park is transferred to the Board, which minister is treated as the ‘Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government’ for applying Part III of the Act?
answer:
Under the certified amendment, for a water supply and sewerage undertaking of an industrial park the words “the Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government” in Part III are read as “the Minister assigned the subject of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka … or the Minister assigned the subject of industries under Article 44 or 45 of the Constitution” as the case may be — i.e. whichever of those two ministers is assigned the subject [Act 20/2026 §10].

- The new section 57A applies Part III “mutatis mutandis” to transfers of such undertakings to the Board [Act 20/2026 §10].
- The same proviso covers an “industrial estate or industrial park” together; it does not differentiate between them [Act 20/2026 §10].
- “Industrial park” is defined by reference to the Industrial Promotion Act, No. 46 of 1990 [Act 20/2026 §19].

Caveats: This is from Act 20/2026, which amends the 1974 Law; the amended Law’s own text is not in evidence, and the proviso does not say how the choice between the two ministers is made.

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill (Gazette text / Bill 2026-10-06, not shown to have passed), the magistrate must act without advance notice to the detention authority [078/2026 §33].

- Must "visit once a month" the approved place of detention, "interview the suspects and look into their well-being", and inspect detention registers, Detention Orders and other documents [078/2026 §33(1)].
- If torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment is observed or alleged, he "shall forthwith make an order" for production before a Judicial Medical Officer and submission of the report [078/2026 §33(4)]; if satisfied on reasonable grounds, he must act under section 31 [078/2026 §33(5)].
- If the centre does not meet humane-treatment requirements, the fact is reported to the Inspector General of Police [078/2026 §34(2)].

Caveats: This is a bill, not law; older bills (e.g. 444/2024 §32) set a weekly visit instead.

question: Under the Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill, which civil or commercial disagreements can be taken to mediation and which types are excluded from this law?
answer:
The evidence is the certified **Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Act, No. 13 of 2026**, not a Bill. It applies to “civil and commercial disputes” mediated under the Act, whether under a mediation agreement, by voluntary referral, or by court referral [Act 13/2026 §2].

- It does **not** apply to mediation under the Mediation Boards Act, No. 72 of 1988 or the Mediation (Special Categories of Disputes) Act, No. 21 of 2003; disputes required to go to those regimes cannot be submitted under this Act [Act 13/2026 §2].
- Mediation is barred where settlement requires terms effective only by court “decree or order,” including disputes in the schedule; related matters may be mediated to submit terms to court [Act 13/2026 §3].

Caveats: The schedule is not reproduced in the evidence, so its listed disputes cannot be identified.

question: What audit regulations govern the financial statements of Samurdhi community‑based banking societies under the Samurdhi amendment?
answer:
Under the Samurdhi (Amendment) Act, No. 15 of 2025 (certified 2025-08-22), audits of samurdhi community based banking societies' accounts must follow the public-corporation audit rules and the National Audit Act.

- The new section 35A applies "Article 154 of the Constitution relating to audit of accounts of public corporations" to those societies [Act 15/2025 §3].
- It also applies "the National Audit Act, No. 19 of 2018" to those audits [Act 15/2025 §3].
- Community based banks are covered separately by new section 28A [Act 15/2025 §2].

Caveats: The Act only states these changes; the full text of the amended Samurdhi Act No. 1 of 2013 is not in evidence.

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
The name in the question matches **Act 12/2025, the Companies (Amendment) Act, No. 12 of 2025** (certified 2025-08-04), an amending Act: its s.17 amends s.487(5) of the principal enactment.

- A struck-off company may, "before the expiry of a period of ten years" from the Act's operation, apply to court with the Attorney-General as a party, showing cause why it could not comply; the court may permit re-registration and order return of property previously vested in the State [Act 12/2025 §17].
- Property otherwise "shall vest in and be at the disposal of the State"; third-party rights acquired in good faith from the State are unaffected [Act 12/2025 §17].
- Where property was destroyed, damaged, or never taken into possession, "the State shall not be liable to any party in any manner" [Act 12/2025 §17].

Caveats: this is an amendment to s.487(5) only — the evidence does not set out s.487(1)/(3) (the strike-off grounds) or a general restoration regime, so the fuller effects on former assets cannot be confirmed. The earlier bill 582/2025 §17 was in similar terms but left the Act's number blank; rely on the Act.

question: Under the revised Anti‑Corruption Act, in what situations will a person charged with a corruption offence be refused bail?
answer:
The evidence does not establish the bail-refusal rule in the Anti-Corruption Act, No. 9 of 2023 as amended; the only bail text is proposed wording that the certified Act did not enact in those words.

- Proposed in bills 051/2026 and 063/2026: no bail "except in exceptional circumstances by a High Court" where a bribe is "not less than one hundred thousand rupees", or a Government loss / benefit of "not less than five hundred thousand rupees" confirmed by the Director-General's certificate — but this was proposed, not enacted in those words in Act 25/2026 [051/2026 §17]; [063/2026 §17].
- The 2023 bills instead provided remand until conclusion of trial, with bail only in "exceptional circumstances" — a proposal, not law [319/2023 §149]; [311/2023 §149].

Caveats: Act 25/2026 amends the principal Act, whose text is not in evidence, so what the amended s.149 now says is unknown.

question: Under the proposed Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters law, how are offences listed in Part B of the extradition schedule treated when Sri Lanka considers extraditing a suspect to another UN member state?
answer:
Under the bill, such Part B offences are deemed **not** to be political offences for extradition purposes. Specifically, they are "deemed not to be an offence of a political character or an offence connected with a political offence or an offence inspired by political motives", and this applies "for the purposes only of extradition" between Sri Lanka and any UN Member State, or of assisting a UN Member State under clause 12 [073/2026 §11].

- This overrides the Extradition Law, No. 8 of 1977 ("Notwithstanding anything in the Extradition Law") [073/2026 §11].
- It is limited to UN Member States, not all requesting states [073/2026 §11].

Caveats: This is a Gazette-text proposal only; no certified Act was found, so it has not been shown to have passed. Note also that clause 8 inserts the new offence *before* Part B, so it sits outside Part B itself [073/2026 §8].

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
Under the National Environmental (Amendment) Act, No. 15 of 2026 (certified 2026-07-21), the substituted penalty for an offence under section 23r(2) is a fine "not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than one million rupees", plus "a fine of five thousand rupees for each day" the offence continues after conviction [Act 15/2026 §18].

- The fine is imposed "on conviction before the Magistrate having jurisdiction" [Act 15/2026 §18].
- The daily Rs. 5,000 charge applies "in the event of the commission of the offence being continued" after conviction [Act 15/2026 §18].

Caveats: This is an amending Act, not the consolidated text of Act No. 47 of 1980; it replaces the earlier figures of Rs. 10,000–100,000 and Rs. 500 per day [Act 15/2026 §18].

question: What penalty does the amendment to the National Audit Act impose for the offence covered by Section 42?
answer:
The amendment substitutes the penalty in section 42 of the principal enactment with "a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees or to an imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding one year or to both such fine and imprisonment" [Act 19/2025 §13].

- This replaces the earlier words "to a fine not less than five thousand rupees and not more than twenty five thousand rupees" [Act 19/2025 §13].
- It is a certified amending Act (No. 19 of 2025, certified 2025-09-22) amending the National Audit Act, No. 19 of 2018 — not the consolidated text of that Act [Act 19/2025 §13].

Caveats: The evidence does not set out what the section 42 offence itself is, only the changed penalty.

question: Under the proposed Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs law, what fine and additional action apply if a dog owner does not vaccinate and register the dog after being given a notice?
answer:
Under the proposed law, a fine of "two thousand rupees" applies, payable in addition to the registration fee due under section 5, and the local authority must itself vaccinate and register the dog "immediately" in the Register of Dogs [076/2026 §7(4)].

- The 14-day notice period (extendable by a further 14 days for reasonable cause) precedes that penalty [076/2026 §7(2)–(3)].

This is from bill 076/2026 (Bill, 2026-09-24); the same clause appears in the 2026-09-07 Gazette text, 066/2026 [066/2026 §7(4)].

Caveats: It is a proposal only — no certified Act held (Acts checked to 2026-10-30), so it has not been shown to have passed.

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:
Under the certified Act, section 54A(1)(a) of the Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance now reads "heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium or methamphetamine" — methamphetamine is added to the named drugs [Act 27/2026 §2].

- New offence: manufacturing any drug in Groups A–E, Part I, Third Schedule other than those five named drugs [Act 27/2026 §2].
- Penalty on conviction by the High Court without a jury: fine "not less than two hundred thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees", or imprisonment "not less than ten years and not exceeding twenty years", or both [Act 27/2026 §2].

Caveats: This is an amending Act, so it states the change only; the Ordinance's full amended text is not in evidence. The same wording appeared in bill 062/2026 [062/2026 §2], now enacted as Act 27/2026.

question: Under the proposed Presidents' Entitlements repeal, will former presidents or their widows keep receiving housing, regular payments, secretarial assistance, official transport or a widow's pension once the new law takes effect?
answer:
No — from the date the Act commences, those benefits stop being provided or paid.

- The Act repeals the Presidents' Entitlements Act, No. 4 of 1986 [Act 18/2025 §2].
- It declares that any residence or monthly allowance (§2 of the repealed Act), monthly secretarial allowance, official transport and other facilities (§3), and the widow's monthly pension (§4) provided before commencement "shall no longer be provided with or paid to, on and after the date of commencement" [Act 18/2025 §3].
- This is a certified Act (2025-09-10), not a bill; it came from bills 624/2025 and 627/2025 [Act 18/2025 §3].

Caveats: Nothing in the evidence states the commencement date itself.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Penal Code, what new penalty is introduced for intentionally causing serious injury to a child under 18?
answer:
The amendment would insert a new section 316a making it an offence to "voluntarily cause[] grievous hurt to a person under eighteen years of age", punishable with "imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years" plus a fine and possible court-ordered compensation, assessed on a victim impact statement from the National Authority for the Protection of Victims of Crime and Witnesses [618/2025 §6].

- This is a bill only (Gazette text 2025-07-08; presented version 630/2025, 2025-08-19); it has not been shown to have passed [618/2025 §6].
- The clause says "voluntarily", not "intentionally"; the "intentionally" wording change in the bill applies to section 308a, the corporal-punishment provision [630/2025; 618/2025 §4].
- Lesser hurt to a child under 314a: up to two years, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both, plus compensation [618/2025 §5].

Caveats: no certified Act is held, so this is a proposed penalty, not law; compensation amounts are set by the court.

question: How does the proposed amendment to the Social Security Contribution Levy Act change the turnover limits and the applicable dates in Section 5, and what new limit is introduced for periods starting on 1 April 2026?
answer:
The evidence does contain the Section 5 amendment, but the enacted version does **not** use 1 April 2026 — the Act moved that date to 1 July 2026.

Act 10/2026 §3 amends Section 5(1) of the principal enactment (the 2022 Act) as follows:
- Paragraph (b): substitutes "hundred and twenty million rupees;" for "hundred and twenty million rupees; or" — i.e. removes the "or" [Act 10/2026 §3(1)].
- Paragraph (c): substitutes "on or after January 1, 2024 and prior to July 1, 2026," and "sixty million rupees; or" for the existing date and "sixty million rupees." [Act 10/2026 §3(2)].
- New paragraph (d): "for any period commencing on or after July 1, 2026", the four-consecutive-quarter turnover must "not exceed thirty-six million rupees" [Act 10/2026 §3(3)].

Caveats: The bill (017/2026 §3, Gazette text 2026-03-03) proposed the same 36 million rupee limit but with "April 1, 2026" dates; that wording was not enacted — the Act's dates are 1 July 2026 [017/2026 §3; Act 10/2026 §3]. No passage gives the pre-amendment text of Section 5 itself, and the evidence does not state the 36 million rupee limit as applying from 1 April 2026.

question: What changes does the amendment to Section 14 of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act make to the ownership percentage requirement and to the type of entities mentioned in its subsections?
answer:
The amendment to Section 14 of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act, No. 36 of 2024 (made by section 12 of the Sri Lanka Electricity (Amendment) Act, No. 14 of 2025 — an Act, certified 2025-08-18) raises the threshold from "more than fifty per centum" to "one hundred per centum" and narrows the actors to companies.

- Subsection (1): "more than fifty per centum" is replaced by "one hundred per centum". [Act 14/2025 §12]
- Subsection (2): "Any person who" is replaced by "Any company incorporated in terms of the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007, which". [Act 14/2025 §12]
- Subsection (3): "a person who" is replaced by "a company, which". [Act 14/2025 §12]

Caveats: The evidence does not reproduce section 14 of the 2024 Act, so what the percentage governs is not shown; it also does not say the word "status"—rather, the amending Act states changes, not the amended text.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Trusts Ordinance, which part of Section 3 is being removed and how is the definition of “express trust” being changed?
answer:
The proposal would repeal paragraph (n) of Section 3 of the Trusts Ordinance (Chapter 87, as last amended by Act No. 6 of 2018), and in paragraph (p) would drop the word "generally" from the "express trust" definition [081/2026 §2].

- Repeal: "by the repeal of paragraph (n) of that section" [081/2026 §2].
- Definition: for "trust generally in the form", substitute "trust in the form" [081/2026 §2].

Caveats: This is Gazette text of the Trusts (Amendment) bill (dated 2026-10-14, same text in 086/2026); it has not been shown to have passed, so it is not law. The content of paragraphs (n) and (p) itself is not in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
The amendment (now law, not a bill) raises one retirement age from 61 to 63 and replaces the other provision so that all other Judges and Magistrates retire at 62. It is section 3 of the Judicature (Amendment) Act, No. 23 of 2026 (certified 2026-09-25), which came from bills 058/2026 and 064/2026 [Act 23/2026 §3].

- Section 6(3) of the principal enactment: substitutes "sixty-three years" for "sixty-one years" [Act 23/2026 §3].
- Section 6(4) is repealed and replaced: "the age of retirement of all other Judges and Magistrates shall be sixty-two years", notwithstanding the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance (Chapter 355) [Act 23/2026 §3].

Caveats: This is an amending Act; the evidence does not show the full text of the amended Judicature Act, and it does not say which judges fall within subsection (3) rather than (4).

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Universities Act, how many terms is a person allowed to serve as dean of a faculty?
answer:
Under the amendment as passed, no person may be **elected Dean of a Faculty for more than two terms** [Act 2/2026 §2(5)].

- The Act inserts this as new subsection (4) of section 49 of the Universities Act, No. 16 of 1978 (the "principal enactment") [Act 2/2026 §2].
- The Gazette text had said "appointed ... for more than two terms"; the certified Act uses "elected", consistent with election by the Faculty Board [Act 2/2026 §2(1)(b), §2(5)].

Caveats: This is an amending Act, so it states the change; the full amended text of section 49 is not in the evidence.

question: What 2025 legislation establishes the professional facilities‑management institute as a legal corporate body in Sri Lanka?
answer:
It is the **Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka (Incorporation)** bill: Gazette text 623/2025 (18 July 2025), presented as Bill 628/2025 (6 August 2025). However, it is only a proposal — no certified Act is held, so it has not been shown to have passed.

- Clause 2(1) constitutes members as a body corporate with "perpetual succession" under that name, able to "sue and be sued" and use a common seal [623/2025 §2 — cited as 623/2025 p.2].
- It would "represent the majority interests of the membership" and uphold professional standards [623/2025 p.2].

Caveats: I used the bill text, not an Act; the auto-generated summaries describing an "Act" are hints only.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 623/2025 §2

question: Which 2025 legislation creates a legal corporation for the charitable foundation named after senior monk Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero?
answer:
No 2025 Act creating that corporation is in the evidence: it appears only as a bill, so incorporation has not been shown to have passed.

- Clause 2 would make the Foundation "a body corporate with perpetual succession" under that name, able to sue, be sued and use a common seal [596/2025 §2].
- Clause 1 gives the intended short title, "...(Incorporation) Act, No. of 2025" [596/2025 §1].
- Two versions exist: Gazette text 581/2025 (2025-04-10) and the presented Bill 596/2025 (2025-05-08); the quoted clauses are identical [581/2025 §2; 596/2025 §2].

Caveats: No certified Act is held (Acts checked to 2026-10-30), so this is a proposal only, not law.

question: What 2026 amendment revises the Act that governs marriage and divorce among the Kandyan community (Chapter 113)?
answer:
The 2026 amendment is the **Kandyan Marriage and Divorce (Amendment)** bill, which amends the Kandyan Marriage and Divorce Act (Chapter 113) by changing Section 32 [008/2026 §2]. It exists as a Gazette text of 2026-02-05 and a presented bill of 2026-02-19 with identical wording [016/2026; 008/2026 §1].

- It substitutes paragraph (a) with “Adultery by the husband or wife after marrige.” [008/2026 §2].
- It repeals paragraph (b) of Section 32 [008/2026 §2].
- No penalty is created; it only revises the grounds [016/2026].

Caveats: this is a proposal only; no certified Act is held (Acts checked to 2026-10-30), so it has not been shown to have passed.

question: What is the 2026 legislation that establishes the Al‑Hashimi Association as a legal corporate entity?
answer:
No such 2026 Act appears in the evidence: it holds only two incorporation **bills**, neither shown to have passed (Acts checked to 2026-10-30). The newest is Bill 039/2026, Al‑Hashimi Association (Incorporation) (Bill, 2026-05-21); an earlier Gazette text is 024/2026 (2026-04-08).

- Both propose that "from and after the date of commencement of this Act" the Association become a body corporate [039/2026 §2(1)] [024/2026 §2(1)].
- Existing debts and liabilities of the Association vest in the new body corporate [039/2026 §12].
- The two versions share the same clause outline (§1–§19) [024/2026 §1].

Caveats: the bill-level summaries describe an "Act" and corporate powers (suing, common seal, property), but those are auto-generated hints; the clause text above is what the evidence supports.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 024/2026 §1, 024/2026 §2, 039/2026 §12, 039/2026 §2

question: Which 2026 bill repeals the 2009 act that created the position of chief of the defence staff in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Act, No. 22 of 2026 (certified 2026-09-22) repeals the Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009: "The Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009 is hereby repealed." [Act 22/2026 §2]

- It is now an Act, not a bill; it came from bill 036/2026 (Gazette text, 2026-05-15) and bill 059/2026 (Bill, 2026-08-04) [Act 22/2026, 036/2026, 059/2026].
- The office holders (Chief of Defence Staff and Committee members) cease to hold office from commencement [Act 22/2026 §3(1)].

Caveats: The evidence describes Act 22/2026 as a repealing Act; it does not set out the 2009 Act's text.

question: What 2025 legislation modifies the 1988 Provincial Councils Elections Act in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2025 measure is the **Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment)** bill — Gazette text published 2025-05-22 (589/2025) and presented as Bill 605/2025 on 2025-06-05. It is a proposal only; no certified Act is held for it, so it has not been shown to have passed.

- It would make the 1988 Act's provisions "in force on September 21, 2017" operative again, "notwithstanding the amendments made thereto by Act, No. 17 of 2017" [589/2025 §2].
- Acts done from 22 September 2017 until commencement are preserved if not inconsistent with the 1988 Act [589/2025 §2].
- Short title: "Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment) Act, No. of 2025" [589/2025 §1].

Caveats: The bill-level summary (auto-generated) also mentions Sinhala text prevailing on inconsistency, but I have not quoted that clause's text.

question: Which 2025 bill amends the 2016 Act that provides a financial assistance scheme for workers?
answer:
The Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment) Act, No. 10 of 2025 — certified on 2025-07-23 and coming from bills 587/2025 (Gazette text, 2025-05-20) and 602/2025 (Bill, 2025-06-03) — amends the Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 4 of 2016 [Act 10/2025 §2].

- It replaces "With effect from May 1, 2015," with a period "commencing on May 1, 2015 and ending on March 31, 2025," and likewise ends the January 1, 2016 period on March 31, 2025 [Act 10/2025 §2].
- The Act's long title states it is "to amend the Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 4 of 2016" [Act 10/2025].

Caveats: The separate National Minimum Wage of Workers (Amendment) Act, No. 11 of 2025 amends a different 2016 Act (No. 3 of 2016) [Act 11/2025 §3]; the §2 amendment is not the amended Act's current text.

question: Which 2025 bill seeks to amend the 2016 legislation that establishes the minimum wage for employees in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2025 bill is the **National Minimum Wage of Workers (Amendment)** bill — Gazette text 586/2025 (2025-05-20), presented as bill 604/2025 (2025-06-03), both stating the purpose "to amend the National Minimum Wage of Workers Act, No. 3 of 2016" [604/2025 §2]. It became **Act No. 11 of 2025** (certified 2025-07-23), so the law is the Act [Act 11/2025].

- The Act substitutes s.3(1): "twenty-seven thousand rupees" monthly until 31 December 2025, then "thirty thousand rupees" from 1 January 2026 [Act 11/2025 §2].
- It is deemed to have come into operation on "April 1, 2025" [Act 11/2025 §1].

Caveats: The amending Act states changes only; the amended 2016 Act's full current text is not in the evidence.

question: Which 2025 amendment alters the 2005 law that established the workers' special financial assistance allowance?
answer:
Act No. 9 of 2025, the Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment) Act, certified 2025-07-23, amends the Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 36 of 2005 [Act 9/2025 §2].

- It substitutes in section 3(1) the words "For the period commencing on August 1, 2005 and ending on March 31, 2025, " for "With effect from August 1, 2005" [Act 9/2025 §2].
- It is deemed to have come into operation on April 1, 2025 [Act 9/2025 §1].
- It came from bills 588/2025 (Gazette text, 2025-05-20) and 603/2025 (Bill, 2025-06-03); those were proposals, so rely on the Act [588/2025].

Caveats: The amending Act states only the change; the amended 2005 Act's full current text is not in evidence.

question: What 2026 legislation proposes to abolish the 1977 law that provided retirement benefits to Sri Lankan parliamentarians?
answer:
The **Parliamentary Pensions (Repeal) Act, No. 5 of 2026** (certified 2026-02-17) — it states: "The Parliamentary Pensions Law, No. 1 of 1977 is hereby repealed" [Act 5/2026 §2].

- It is an Act, passed from bill 001/2026 (presented 2026-01-07) [Act 5/2026; 001/2026].
- That bill was a proposal at the time; rely on the Act for the enacted wording [001/2026 §4].

Caveats: the evidence does not set out the Act's commencement date or the detailed effect on existing pension payments; the summary touching those points is auto-generated only [Act 5/2026].

question: Which 2025 bill sought to modify the 1988 Sri Lankan law that imposes a tax on gambling activities?
answer:
Bill **640/2025** (Gazette text, 2 October 2025) and its presented version **642/2025** (Bill, 21 October 2025) both became **Act No. 25/2025** (certified 17 December 2025), amending the Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No. 40 of 1988 [640/2025; 642/2025; Act 25/2025 §2].

- The Act sets the 15% rate for years commencing on or after 1 April 2023 "but ending prior to January 1, 2026", and adds a new 18% rate for years from 1 January 2026 [Act 25/2025 §2].
- It raises the stated amount in subsection (1AA) from "United States Dollars fifty" to "one hundred" [Act 25/2025 §2].

Caveats: the bills' auto-generated summaries say 18% from 1 October 2025, but the Act says 1 January 2026 — rely on the Act [Act 25/2025 §2].

question: Which 2025 bill proposes changes to the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464)?
answer:
Two 2025 bills in the evidence amend the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464), with identical clause text: 617/2025 (Gazette text, 4 July 2025) and 625/2025 (Bill, 22 July 2025). Both are proposals, not law.

- Each repeals "or upon his or her marriage" in subsection 48A 2(c) [617/2025 §2; 625/2025 §2].
- Each repeals subsection 48B 1(a) [625/2025 §3].
- Each substitutes "fails without reasonable cause to succeed" in section 68(1) [617/2025 §4; 625/2025 §4].

Caveats: The evidence does not show which of the two was the operative or later version, nor their long titles; neither is shown to have passed.

question: Which 2026 bill updates the 2018 Finance Act No. 35?
answer:
The **Finance (Amendment)** bill amends section 44 of the Finance Act, No. 35 of 2018 — Gazette text 027/2026 (2026-04-23) and Bill 034/2026 (2026-05-06) carry identical text [034/2026 §2].

- It substitutes wording in s.44(1) to exempt "any newly constructed cellular tower" commencing commercial operations on or after January 1, 2026, "for a period of five years" [034/2026 §2(1)].
- s.44(2) is amended to make levy payment "Subject to the provisions of subsection (1)" [034/2026 §2(2)].

Caveats: Both are proposals only; no certified Act was held (Acts checked to 2026-10-30), so passage is not shown [034/2026 §2].

question: Which 2026 bill revises the 1956 law that sets rules for female workers, teenage employees and child labor?
answer:
The Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) bill — Gazette text 044/2026 (25 June 2026), then Bill 056/2026 (22 July 2026) — which became Act No. 21 of 2026 (certified 8 September 2026), amending Act No. 47 of 1956 [044/2026] [056/2026] [Act 21/2026 §1].

- It substitutes "one hundred thousand rupees" for "ten thousand rupees" in sections 7(3) and 13(2) [Act 21/2026 §2] [Act 21/2026 §3].
- The higher amounts do not apply to offences committed before the Act came into operation [Act 21/2026 §5].

Caveats: The evidence does not include the full text of the 1956 Act, and the section 20A(3) amendment appears only in the summaries, not quoted clause text.

question: Which 2025 bill proposes to revoke the 2024 legislation that introduced internet safety and content regulation measures?
answer:
The **Online Safety (Repeal) Bill** — Bill 590/2025 (Bill, 2025-05-08); an earlier Gazette text is 578/2025 (2025-04-08). It has not been shown to have passed, as no certified Act is held for it [590/2025].

- Clause 2: "The Online Safety Act, No. 9 of 2024 is hereby repealed" [578/2025 §2].
- Clause 3: regulations made under that Act after its enactment are also repealed from the date this Act is enacted [590/2025 §3].
- Short title: "Online Safety (Repeal) Act, No. of 2025" [590/2025 §1].

Caveats: Both versions are proposals only, not law; the wording of the two is identical on these clauses.

question: What 2025 legislation addresses re‑conducting postponed local council elections by allowing new nominations and setting a fresh election date?
answer:
The **Local Authorities Elections (Special Provisions) Act, No. 1 of 2025** (certified 17 February 2025, from bills 565/2025 and 566/2025) is the 2025 law: it voids the earlier nominations for the listed postponed councils and provides for fresh nominations and elections.

- Nomination papers submitted for the 9 March 2023 elections to the scheduled authorities are "deemed to be of no force and effect as if such nomination papers had never been submitted", and the related notices under section 38(1) of the Ordinance are revoked [Act 1/2025 §2].
- Fresh nomination notices under section 26 of the Ordinance are to be published on a date the Election Commission determines by Gazette Order, "not later than three months from the date of coming into operation of this Act" [Act 1/2025 §3].

Caveats: the Act sets a deadline for the *nomination notices*, not a fixed polling date; the election date itself is not stated in the evidence.

question: Which 2025 bill updates the 2008 act that governs major strategic development projects in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2025 update is the **Strategic Development Projects (Amendment) Bill**: Bill **650/2025** (Bill, 14 Nov 2025), following Gazette text **643/2025** (7 Nov 2025); both became **Act No. 26 of 2025** (certified 17 Dec 2025) [650/2025] [643/2025].

question: Which 2026 bill was introduced to legally establish the UnV charitable foundation?
answer:
The **UnV Foundation (Incorporation)** bill: **010/2026**, presented 2026-01-22 (Gazette text **003/2026**, 2026-01-09). It is a bill, not law — no certified Act is held for it, so it has not been shown to have passed [010/2026 §1].

- Its long title is "An Act to incorporate the UnV Foundation", reciting that the foundation "has heretofore been established in Sri Lanka" and applied to be incorporated [010/2026].
- On commencement, the existing foundation's debts and liabilities pass to the new body corporate [010/2026 §12].

Caveats: Clause text for 010/2026 and 003/2026 is stated to be identical; only the bill-level summary describes the committee/governance detail.

question: Which 2025 bill updates Sri Lanka's 1979 criminal procedure legislation?
answer:
Bill 576/2025 — Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) (Gazette text, 28 March 2025) — is the 2025 bill amending the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979; it became Act No. 7 of 2025 (certified 20 June 2025), so the Act is the law to rely on [576/2025] [Act 7/2025].

- The Act inserts new sections 144A and 144B into the 1979 Code, letting a Magistrate dispense with a suspect's or accused's personal attendance for detention extension, bail, investigation assistance "or any other purpose" [Act 7/2025 §2].
- Grounds include threats to life, breach of peace, escape risk, quarantine and compulsory rehabilitation [Act 7/2025 §2].
- It also amends the Second Schedule, inserting Forms 24 and 25 on service abroad of commissions [Act 7/2025 §6].

Caveats: the Act's provenance note lists bill 576/2025 and 579/2025; the 2024 bills (524/2024, 550/2024) are not law per the evidence.

question: What 2026 bill proposes the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution?
answer:
Bill 065/2026, the **Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution** (Bill, 2026-08-18), presented by the Minister of Justice and National Integration; an earlier Gazette text version is 057/2026 (2026-08-07) [065/2026 §1][057/2026 §1]. Neither is law — no certified Act is held for it (Acts checked to 2026-10-30), so it has not been shown to have passed [065/2026; 057/2026].

- It replaces Article 107(5): Supreme Court judges retire at "sixty-seven years", Court of Appeal judges at "sixty-five years", and the Chief Justice retires at 67 or six years after appointment, "whichever occurs earlier" [065/2026 §2].
- It amends Article 137, substituting "not more than twenty four other Judges" for "not more than nineteen" [065/2026 §3].
- Sinhala text prevails over Tamil [057/2026 §4].

Caveats: the auto-generated summary of 065/2026 garbles the retirement-age change ("67 to 67"); the clause text above is authoritative.

question: Which 2026 bill seeks to repeal the 1972 Tenancy Act (No. 7) in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Rent (Repeal) Bill 006/2026 (2026-01-20)** — note it is the **Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972**, not a "Tenancy Act" — repeals that Act: "The Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972 is hereby repealed" [006/2026 §2].

- It is a bill, and has not been shown to have passed (no certified Act held; Acts checked to 2026-10-30) [006/2026 §2].
- Repeal is qualified: for one year from the "relevant date", no ejectment of tenants and no rent above the authorised rent [006/2026 §3(a)–(b)].
- Identical text appeared earlier in the Rent (Repeal) Gazette text 526/2024 (2024-07-19) and 555/2024 [526/2024 §3].

Caveats: No 2026 bill repealing a "Tenancy Act" appears in the evidence; the title-matching 2026 bill is the Rent (Repeal) Bill above.

question: What 2026 legislation creates a corporate entity for the Mahawilachchiya children’s education centre?
answer:
The matching 2026 proposal is the **Mahawilachchiya Education Centre for Children (Incorporation)** bill — Gazette text 011/2026 (2026-02-06), with identical text in the presented Bill 015/2026 (2026-02-18). It has not been shown to have passed; no certified Act is held (Acts checked to 2026-10-30).

- §2(1) constitutes the existing members as a body corporate with "perpetual succession" under the name "Mahawilachchiya Centre for Education for Children", able to sue and be sued and to use a common seal [011/2026 §2].

Caveats: it is a bill, not law; the two versions differ only in publication stage (Gazette text vs Bill).
